credited.title: Nominal reads may write
credited.basis: THE STRONGEST STATEMENT OF THIS PROPOSITION IN THE EXPERIMENT, and this arm reached it TWICE from two different leads. J0021 R1.2 ('Seven "read" commands are native writers, and the schema structurally forbids them a writer lease'): it quotes the frozen schema's command_request allOf[2] verbatim - the seven IDs cmd.jujutsu.{status.refresh, diff.open, history.open, workspace.list, workspace.open, operation.log, operation.show} forced to writer_lease_ref: null - against jj's own documentation that 'Most jj commands you run will commit the working-copy changes if they have changed' and that a snapshot 'gets recorded as an operation', and against CommandHelper::resolve_operation reaching op_heads_store::resolve_op_heads independent of ignore-working-copy. It then names the enumerated effect set the union asks for: the snapshot operation, the 'reconcile divergent operations' merge, and Git ref import (PR #9829, unmerged at 0.44.0, 'jj git fetch and jj git import could turn a change divergent ... most often a working-copy snapshot'). J0028 A1 reaches the same proposition from lead rank 14 with the v0.44.0 CLI reference text and RepoLoader::load_at_head, and adds the self-invalidating-fence consequence: the read carries currentness.expected_operation_id, and executing it the default way changes the op head, so the fence invalidates itself.

credited.title: Writer authority is stronger than native locks
credited.basis: J0021 R1.3 states it as a modelling gap with the native mechanism named: 'A non-Puppet-Master jj writer is not modeled anywhere.' JJI-004's two-mutation-authorities rule is scoped to JJ versus Git; $defs.writer_lease is 'a purely PM-internal record ... with no native counterpart and no field for an observed foreign writer'; the op-heads lock is advisory and jj documents it as 'not needed for correctness'; both writers succeed and the next load merges. The arm then states the obligation in the exact form the union asks for: 'A writer lease is authority over Puppet Master's own dispatch only; it does not exclude a native Jujutsu process, and the adapter detects that case from operation-head divergence rather than from lease state', with foreign_native_operation_observed added to both closed vocabularies and the realistic foreign writers named (the user's CLI, a second editor integration, an fsmonitor/Watchman trigger).

credited.title: Expected operation is not native compare-and-swap
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap. J0021 R1.1 is the proposition: the fence is check-then-act, '--at-operation binds a historical read, disables snapshotting, and FORKS on mutation rather than rejecting. Therefore passing an expected operation as --at-op does not implement stale-command rejection.' The mechanism is named from source - update_op_heads(&self, old_ids, new_id) has 'no expected-value parameter, no conflict return' - and jj's own concurrency doc is quoted: 'The operation cannot fail to commit ... It is left for the next command to notice if there were divergent operations.' The repair requires exactly what the union proposition requires: re-verification of the published operation's parent set after the effect, with outcome forced to recovery_required or effect_unknown when the lineage is not linear from the expected operation.

credited.title: Exact durable identity and operation-local selectors
credited.basis: J0022 L-21de7aceefe8 separates the identities and shows one of them silently substituted. The frozen contract requires change_id, commit_id, operation_id, workspace_id and bookmarks as required non-empty strings with additionalProperties false and 'no provenance, confidence or "synthesized" marker on change_id'. The arm then shows that after extras-marker loss 'affected commits acquire a synthesized change ID (bit-reversed commit ID) and an empty predecessor list, and every read afterwards succeeds', so 'the frozen acceptance criteria pass while the identity the owner calls canonical has silently changed' - because JJI-002 compares the expected operation and IMMUTABLE COMMIT identity, and commit_id is the Git OID and is unaffected. The repair forbids emitting such a revision as canonical change identity.
code_fact_verification: V-P17 docs/technical/architecture.md:82-86 @ e6dd2c0 - 'For commits that don't have any data in that table, which is any commit created by git, we use an empty list as predecessors, and the bit-reversed commit ID as change ID.' VERIFIED VERBATIM. This is the load-bearing impact sentence.

credited.title: Process failure and cancellation are not no-effect proof
credited.basis: J0027 L-f0795b00764c states it as a contract defect: 'a failed result carrying after_revision: null and receipt_ref: null is schema-valid today, which would represent a durable rewritten commit and a new operation as "nothing happened"', and 'Nothing in the corpus instructs a consumer that a nonzero backend exit may still carry a durable effect.' The owner prose it proposes is the proposition: 'A nonzero adapter outcome does not establish that no native mutation occurred; when the adapter can read a new operation identity, the result is failed with effect_state=known_applied, the exact after operation identity, and a receipt.' Repair 6 supplies the reconciliation mechanism - re-read the operation head and compare with the recorded before operation ID; a changed head establishes known_applied, an unchanged head known_not_applied, and only an unreadable head may be effect_unknown. J0021 R2.3 adds the multi-stage half: 'One user-visible recovery appends several operations; before/after cannot represent it.'

credited.title: Partial multi-file resolve
credited.basis: J0027 L-f0795b00764c repair 4 states it and grounds it in an in-corpus precedent rather than inventing one: 'For any owner command whose native implementation applies per-path or per-target work non-atomically, the terminal receipt identifies exactly which units were applied (not only how many) - the analogue of "Partial fan-out identifies exactly which ref reached each target".' Repair 5 adds the retry rule - a known_applied failure sets retry_disposition after_user_action, 'the remaining conflicted paths are re-resolvable, but a blind re-dispatch must not be automatic' - which is the union's 'preserve earlier accepted resolutions ... rather than claiming the entire resolve did nothing'.

credited.title: Native versus sidecar crash boundary
credited.basis: Two halves, both stated. Independent observability across partial failure: J0028 B1 shows the closed vocabularies cannot express four distinct classes and names them - unsupported repository layout, missing object closure, 'a damaged/truncated store reason (zero-length object or op-store files)', and repository maintenance failed - 'Everything in those four classes collapses into adapter_failed, transport_unavailable, or repository_quarantined, which is precisely the conflation the lead warns about.' Do-not-trust-a-healthy-looking-graph: J0022 establishes that on an empty marker directory both accessors do MutableTable::full + save_table, so 'an empty marker directory is silently treated as a FRESH STORE, never as damage', and after the loss 'the op log is complete, no object is missing, the object format is supported, and get_head() returns a valid (empty) table without error.'

credited.title: Native recovery has explicit scope
credited.basis: J0021 R3.5 is the proposition applied to a scope the corpus does not separate: 'The workspace registry is outside the operation log, so undo/op restore do not restore it.' J0018's reconciliation supplies the general form - 'recovery is a multi-operation writer, not a repair-in-place' - and J0021 R2.1 establishes that 'there is no typed reason for a stale working copy, and jj routes three distinct remedies', which is the union's requirement that undo, inverse-one-operation, full-view restore, workspace path recovery and external-file recovery stay distinct.

credited.title: Stale workspace recovery
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap, and stated across five numbered repairs. R2.1: 'There is no typed reason for a stale working copy, and jj routes three distinct remedies.' R2.2 is the destructive-refresh clause exactly: 'snapshot.auto-update-stale can turn a blocked command into a silent multi-operation recovery. Require explicit per-invocation suppression.' R2.4 is the do-not-guess-the-newest-operation clause: 'Fresh does not mean "same operation", and Updated reloads the repo backwards' - the arm establishes the native freshness taxonomy is four-valued, not the two-valued model the corpus assumes. R2.5 adds that the colocated update-stale Git-HEAD defect is in the frozen 0.44.0 profile and is not disclosed.

credited.title: Empty, absent and failed reads are distinct
credited.basis: J0028 C1 states the failed-native-query clause exactly: 'a failed graph query can validate as a clean empty page' - a projection with returned_count 0, has_more false and currentness.state current 'validates today', so 'an adapter whose jj log aborted (panic, process abort) could legally render "no history" as current and complete'. Repair 3 is the union's obligation in one line: 'Backend abort is failed, never empty: a crashed backend query maps to the command result failed with effect_state: none; the history surface shows a failure state with a retry action, not an empty graph.'

credited.title: External editor path confinement
credited.basis: J0027 cross-cutting finding F-C plus L-c16f21f72e55. F-C is the mechanism: FileSafe's write-scope model 'is a pre-spawn path check, not a constraint on what a spawned tool writes' - canonicalize-then-compare applied to paths 'Puppet Master itself declares before spawn', which 'neither constrains where a spawned process writes afterwards, [n]or addresses a path that becomes a symlink between the check and the write'. The lead then states the consequence the union proposition names: rejecting the editor's nonzero exit 'cannot undo a file already written through a link outside the tree - so the natural "we ignored the tool's output" mitigation is not a mitigation for this class'.

credited.title: External diff and merge tool handoff
credited.basis: J0027 L-c16f21f72e55's repair is the managed session: adapter-invoked interactive commands run with the tool pinned to jj's built-in editor supplied by the adapter's own process-scoped configuration, never inheriting ambient ui.diff-editor / ui.merge-editor / merge-tools.* configuration; a third-party tool becomes 'a separate, typed, disabled-by-default capability' reporting state=blocked with a new closed reason code; and the receipt records tool identity, invocation mode (dir / file-by-file), whether an $output tree was supplied, the temp-tree root ref, and the temp-tree disposition (imported / discarded / cleanup_unproven). That last enum is the union's requirement that readiness, save, exit, cancel and cleanup are tracked separately.

credited.title: Adapter implementation shape
credited.basis: J0021 P1.2 is the proposition, posed as an owner decision and explicitly not assumed: 'decide the adapter binding (jj CLI subprocess vs. jj-lib linkage)'. It shows the corpus is 'undecided in §3.3 and CLI-shaped in §3.2' - §3.3 says no schema field assigns a direct subprocess, while §3.2 requires the receipt to carry 'exact command argv identity without secrets', and 'an argv is a subprocess artifact'. It then tabulates six capabilities that depend on the choice (operation stamping via Transaction::set_attribute, foreign-writer identification, is_snapshot classification, the freshness taxonomy, auto-update-stale suppression, and the argv receipt field), names the hybrid option, and records API churn as the cost - keeping all consumers behind one owner throughout.

credited.title: Effective config and template parsing
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap, AND REACHED BY NO CONTINUATION-4 ARM. J0020 P1 states the config-precedence half of the proposition with its mechanism: immutable_heads() and trunk() are revset aliases resolved from configuration, the documented way to set trunk() per repository is jj config set --repo, and that per-repo layer is exactly what secure-config relocates OUT of the repository - so 'Sanitizing (R2) or failing to load that layer therefore SILENTLY CHANGES which commits are trunk and which are immutable.' The gap is stated against the fence: 'PM's revision fence binds change/commit/operation/workspace/bookmarks but NO CONFIGURATION IDENTITY, so two reads of the same repository under different effective configuration carry identical fences and different answers about immutability.' The repair adds an effective_config_ref digest over the layers actually in effect plus a config_layers_present classification and a typed blocker.
credited.clause_coverage: Credited on the config-precedence clause, which the arm states completely and grounds in shipped 0.44.0 behaviour. The proposition's second clause - forcing explicit machine templates and escaping - is NOT addressed anywhere in this arm's corpus. Disclosed rather than silently allowed, on the same basis as the F092 disclosures in continuation 4.

credited.title: Native conflict truth and supported shape
credited.basis: THE BEST STATEMENT OF THIS PROPOSITION IN THE EXPERIMENT. J0027 L-6ab2467deb87 shows the corpus's only conflict-resolution surface contradicting JJI-005 in three independent ways: (1) a Git-marker scan does not detect jj's DEFAULT diff-style sections, so 'a still-conflicted file therefore reads as "no conflict markers remain"'; (2) fixed-length marker matching is wrong in both directions because jj lengthens markers when content could collide; (3) 'Jujutsu has NO "mark resolved" state to set: resolution is inferred from the bytes at snapshot time', so a mark-resolved action is a Git-index concept the corpus already forbids in JJ mode. Point (b) is the supported-shape clause: ours|theirs|both 'cannot express a Jujutsu conflict' because jj supports arbitrarily many sides, and 'Applying "ours" to a 3-sided jj conflict has no defined meaning.'

credited.title: Exact-profile conflict byte regression
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap. J0027 L-6ab2467deb87 (e) states it as a property of the certified version: 'The pinned certification version is a known byte-fidelity risk. The Plans' 0.44.0 profile is precisely the range in which a materialize->parse round trip drops a trailing CR, and the fix commit's own message explains the consequence - update_from_content's unchanged-check compares parsed hunks against stored ones, so the missing byte reads as a real edit and gets written.' It then names the contract consequence: 'That directly undercuts JJI-005's "prove current snapshot, expected conflict identity"', and the arm's repair requires the marker style and byte fidelity to be disclosed rather than assumed.

credited.title: Graph bounds, continuity and isolation
credited.basis: J0028 C2 states the selection clause against the owning contract: selection_anchor_preserved and stable_node_identity are literal const: true, 'the projection ASSERTS them', while the native mechanism that would deliver anchoring is unusable across the version boundary - on 0.44.0 the prioritize/visibility mismatch panics, and from 0.45.0 it is 'a SILENT NO-OP with no warning'. The repair makes it a projection-side obligation verified by the adapter: 'after building a page, the adapter must confirm the selected node is present in nodes (or that has_more/cursor state truthfully explains its absence) and must not rely on a backend prioritize/ordering hint. If the anchor cannot be proven present, the page is partial, not current.' C1 supplies the partial-exposure half - a failed query may never present as current.
credited.clause_coverage: Credited on two of the proposition's four clauses - preserve geometry and selection, and expose missing/partial state - both stated against the owning schema with acceptance fixtures. The cursor-isolation and operation/projection-identity binding clauses are not stated. Disclosed.

credited.title: Hidden graph regression qualification
credited.basis: GAINED OVER claude-hicap, AND REACHED BY NO CONTINUATION-4 ARM. J0028 C1 is the proposition exactly: test prioritized/hidden-revision graph queries against the exact supported native version. The arm establishes the frozen profile is affected by direct code comparison at the tag - 'At the v0.44.0 tag the pre-fix sequence is present verbatim - cli/src/commands/log.rs:186-188, prio_revset.intersect_with(...) with no within_visibility scope - and lib/src/graph.rs:304 is the panic site itself' - and that the hazardous shape is ON BY DEFAULT because log-graph-prioritize = "present(@)" is the shipped default. It then requires a version-pinned known-defect gate with its own typed code, explicitly modelled on the existing jj_0_44_colocated_import_export_disabled_upstream_race precedent, and records that the post-fix behaviour is a silent no-op rather than a diagnostic.

credited.title: Sanitized inactive restore configuration
credited.basis: J0020 R2 states the proposition and shows why the frozen acceptance would pass while the hazard is untested: under 0.44.0 the repo config lives outside the repository and 'what the backup carries is the 20-hex-character id file', so 'A sanitizer that scans restored bytes finds nothing and can truthfully emit sanitized_inactive, while the activated copy proceeds to resolve that id ON THE RESTORING MACHINE - including fix.tools.* command execution'. The arm also establishes the correct inert action rather than just naming the requirement: blanking or truncating the id file 'bricks every command in the restored copy' because maybe_load_config rejects a non-20-character or non-hex id, so 'deleting the file is the inert, correct action'. R4 adds the capture-side link policy for the legacy config symlink.

credited.title: Partial clone and LFS/submodule eligibility
credited.basis: J0026 L-732df4469871 gives partial/promisor its explicit qualification and closure disposition and states the never-silently-hydrate clause as the primary repair. R1: 'define "read-only Git inspection" as provably non-fetching ... an object that is not locally present is reported as a typed absence, never fetched. A read capability never authorizes a network fetch or a local object-store write.' R2 makes filtered state an eligibility and closure input with a four-valued backing_store_filter_state and a new closed reason code, noting that promisor_marked or filter_configured must fail mutation eligibility closed. R3 separates promised absence from damage using --missing=allow-promisor, and R5 records that a clean fsck does not prove local presence. Submodules and shallow clones are qualified from jj's own compatibility table.

credited.title: Authorized incomplete-object materialization
credited.basis: J0026 records it as a product proposal requiring approval and keeps it out of the repair, which is the union's framing: 'a separately authorized pre-capture hydration capability'. It is the necessary complement to R1's non-fetching rule - once reads are proven non-fetching, obtaining the missing promisor objects for inspection or for a complete retained-history backup has to become an explicit authorized act rather than a side effect of a read.

credited.title: Operation metadata is not idempotency
credited.basis: The lead's own title is the proposition: 'Native operation attributes can correlate work, but are not an idempotency protocol.' J0028 A3 develops the durability half - 'the native args attribute is durable user text inside the repository' - and A4 proposes an adapter-owned correlation attribute plus two-phase publication for effect_unknown, keeping the durable command-instance identity on PM's side rather than inferring it from native operation metadata. J0021 R1.1 supplies the operation-lineage half: an after-operation identity alone cannot establish that the intended command produced it, which is why the parent set has to be compared.

partial_matches.title: Terminal attempts always have receipts
partial_matches.why_partial: J0027 L-f0795b00764c repair 1 requires a non-null receipt_ref - but only in the conditional case where outcome is failed/cancelled/recovery_required AND error.effect_state == known_applied. F001 requires a non-null owner receipt for EVERY terminal attempt, including effect-unknown results, which this arm does not state. The arm is closer to this correction than any continuation-4 review arm except claude-hicap, and it is refused on the same test I applied to those five.

partial_matches.title: Hunk and editable diff safety
partial_matches.why_partial: J0027 L-c16f21f72e55 binds an external editable-diff session to a pinned tool, a temp-tree root ref and a typed disposition, and F-C establishes that FileSafe cannot constrain what the spawned tool writes. What it does not state is the proposition's own content: binding partial-edit SELECTIONS to both rendered sides, to native conflict state, to an exact session/repository/revision, and to complete matched selections. The arm's leads never reached the hunk-selection material.

partial_matches.title: Queue reentrancy and dependency deadlocks
partial_matches.why_partial: J0021 R1.4 establishes that the Git import/export lock is repo-wide at 0.44.0 and that 'a stalled fsmonitor query in one workspace held it for the fsmonitor timeout. In both cases every jj status in every other workspace queued behind it', and requires a waiting_on_native_lock degraded reason so the GUI can say why Source Control is not refreshing. That is native lock contention made visible. F071's proposition is about PM's own nested queue and lock acquisition deadlocking refresh, editor, authentication or mutation completion, which the arm does not address.

partial_matches.title: Read preview and dry-run side effects
partial_matches.why_partial: J0028 A1 point 5 gets close - 'if a dispatch observes "Concurrent modification detected, resolving automatically" ... that is a repository mutation and cannot be reported as a clean read' - and the whole of R1.2/A1 is about a read LABEL not matching the effect. But the proposition's subjects are preview, dry-run and immutable-override retry being taken as read-only or newly authorized because a client labels them so, and none of those three is examined. Credited as F002, which is what the arm actually proves.

That is two of F107's four clauses - relational validation of the emitted page, and unambiguous node identity/anchoring. The usable-continuation clause and the finite parent-reference expansion policy are not stated. muse13 was credited at 3 of 4 with the gap disclosed and claude-hicap at 4 of 4; 2 of 4 is below that bar.
